title: Compound Interest & Time Value of Money
content:
Compound interest is the addition of interest to the principal sum of a loan or deposit, or in other words, interest on interest. Using the formula A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt), investors harness exponential growth over multi-decade horizons. The Rule of 72 (72 / annual return %) estimates how many years it takes to double an investment. Starting early reduces the monthly savings required to hit retirement milestones by more than 50%.

Key Beginner Takeaway: Understanding compound interest & time value of money helps investors make disciplined, evidence-based decisions aligned with their time horizon and risk tolerance. Always prioritize low fees, broad diversification, and tax efficiency before attempting complex strategies.

Investors must distinguish between capacity for risk (financial ability to absorb losses) and tolerance for risk (psychological comfort with market drops).

title: Inflation and Purchasing Power Erosion
content:
Inflation measures the rate at which the general price level of goods and services rises, eroding purchasing power. If inflation averages 3% annually, $100,000 today buys only $55,368 worth of goods in 20 years. Holding excessive cash in low-yield checking accounts leads to guaranteed real wealth loss, making inflation-beating assets like equities, TIPS, and real estate essential for long-term goals.

Key Beginner Takeaway: Understanding inflation and purchasing power erosion helps investors make disciplined, evidence-based decisions aligned with their time horizon and risk tolerance. Always prioritize low fees, broad diversification, and tax efficiency before attempting complex strategies.
